# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected for a child her age when engaging in physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets much faster than expected for a child her age when playing outside or running around, which has been a concern for the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be picky with food and will refuse to eat certain things from time to time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears to get tired quickly when engaging in physical activities, and even simple tasks like going for a short walk can exhaust her sooner than her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with fluid buildup in her ears and has been taken to see specialists several times because of this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on things, which makes the parents worry if there's something wrong with her eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip very easily, and the parents have to keep a close eye on her dental health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's dental health and prevent further tooth breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any issues related to fluid buildup in the ears.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and address any issues related to squinting or other vision problems.
* Cardiac review to assess the patient's heart health and address any concerns related to faster breathing during physical activities.
* Consider referral for a skeletal review to assess the patient's spinal bones and address any concerns related to curvature of the spine or short fingers.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioural differences.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired fast when playing outside, and her energy levels seem lower than those of her friends, indicating potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, as she often asks her parents to repeat themselves, indicating potential conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her daily life, particularly when trying to focus on things close up or reading.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods, which causes her discomfort.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to investigate potential skeletal anomalies
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) if clinical concerns arise

## 1) RESPIRATORY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in his heart, which requires regular check-ups to monitor the situation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slow weight gain and has had feeding difficulties, which are being monitored to ensure he is getting enough nutrients.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are being managed with the help of his doctors to reduce their frequency.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to hear some sounds but not others clearly, and has required multiple ear infections and possible conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the TV or books, which makes his parents worry about his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, even when eating normal food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and seems behind other children in development, which are areas being worked on with therapists and his healthcare team.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers and curved 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent further breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any potential conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and address any potential vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Seizure management to reduce the frequency and severity of the patient's seizures.
* Speech therapy to address the patient's speech delay and support his developmental progress.
* Occupational therapy to support the patient's fine motor development and daily living skills.
* Physiotherapy to support the patient's gross motor development and overall physical health.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, unfortunately. There's an abnormality with one of the valves. We go back to the cardiologist regularly for check-ups. They monitor it closely to ensure everything stays stable. As a parent, it's terrifying to think about, but we're managing so far.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He was born with a tethered cord. That's meant lots of monitoring over time to ensure no lasting damage occurred. So far, touch wood, he seems okay, though we do have regular scans to confirm.

Parent: N/A.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in his ear, causing discomfort and pain, and has undergone treatments to clear it out.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, with his eyes turned inward slightly, affecting his everyday life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that was identified early on and is being tracked by a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble latching on and keeping food down as an infant, indicating feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears to have coordination issues, seeming less steady on his feet compared to peers, and has trouble getting his words out clearly when trying to communicate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets upset in very noisy environments, and loud noises really frustrate him, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs frequent dental checks to prevent further problems, and the dentist says this is necessary.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble getting his words out clearly when trying to communicate, and appears to have coordination issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may experience developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has undescended testicles.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience short fingers and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to prevent further dental problems
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Consideration of a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns
* Referral for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address coordination and communication issues
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired very easily and seems to run out of energy much quicker compared to her peers, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had significant feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and getting frustrated easily, although this has mostly resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with her spinal cord being tethered, which is being monitored by doctors to see if any intervention might be needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have hearing difficulties, particularly with background noise, and may have issues with sound sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently, especially when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods, and has had challenges finding toothpaste she can tolerate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, with some needing specialist SEN dentists.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with speech, having difficulty getting words out clearly and finding the right things to say.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel health.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to check for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess for heart conditions.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental and speech difficulties.
* Regular monitoring of the tethered spinal cord issue to determine if intervention is required.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in her heart, which requires regular check-ups for monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, including constipation and diarrhea, and has difficulty finding foods that agree with her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has seizures, which are controlled with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in her ear, which may affect her hearing, and has trouble seeing the board at school due to vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board at school and squints or gets closer to see what's written.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods, such as apples or meat, due to jaw pain.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably different posture when standing or walking, and has been diagnosed with scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor spinal health
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and behaviour
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

Parent: She had fluid in her ear last winter and needed antibiotics to clear it up. Since then, we haven't had any more issues with her ears.

Parent: Cold foods and drinks seem to really bother her teeth - she complains they feel sensitive. It started happening around her second birthday and has continued since.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When our little girl plays outside or runs around, her breathing gets much faster than we expect. At first, we thought maybe she was just very active, but after monitoring it closely, we realized it happens almost every time she exerts herself physically.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: During playtime or even simple tasks like walking upstairs, our daughter tends to get unusually tired. This concern came up because other kids her age seem to handle these activities without needing such frequent breaks.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: There's definitely a feeding aversion - certain tastes or textures make her push food away. It started early on and persists; sometimes mealtimes become battles because of this issue.

Parent: Two significant ones - our child has shown signs of speech delay; she doesn't form sentences like other three-year-olds do. Additionally, there's a hip issue - diagnosed as hip dysplasia. Regular appointments with specialists help monitor both conditions closely.

Parent: The cardiologist found a structural abnormality in her heart. We go for regular check-ups to make sure everything is okay and that it doesn't affect her daily life too much.

Parent: N/A

Parent: N/A

Parent: Well... developmentally, she seems behind other kids her age. It takes her longer to learn new skills and reach milestones. We're working with therapists to support her development and hoping she'll catch up soon.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in her heart, which requires regular check-ups to ensure it does not affect her daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, with certain textures and tastes she won't tolerate, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and must take medication regularly to prevent seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond right away when called, and there are concerns about possible hearing problems, although tests have not shown anything conclusive yet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and uses glasses to correct it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and require regular dental check-ups, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind other kids her age, taking longer to learn new skills and reach milestones, and is working with therapists for support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind other kids her age and has a feeding aversion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for possible hearing problems
* Regular check-ups with the cardiologist to monitor the structural abnormality in the heart
* Continued medication and monitoring for epilepsy
* Ongoing support and therapy for developmental delay and feeding aversion
* Regular monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular check-ups with a cardiologist to ensure stability.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a significant feeding aversion, making mealtime challenging, and requires exploration of ways to make eating more comfortable and enjoyable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including slower progress in reaching milestones like walking or sitting, and is working with a pediatric neurologist to address these delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, ranging from mild to severe, with most having some degree of developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with glue ear, leading to repeated ear infections and some hearing difficulties, and is working with an ENT specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children require multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint, affecting his ability to focus on distant objects, which may impact his learning and overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger-than-usual front teeth, causing difficulties with biting and chewing food properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia of upper central incisors), and may experience weak enamel, requiring careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delays and feeding aversion may impact his learning and educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans due to more significant learning difficulties.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty making himself understood when communicating, affecting his social interactions and learning processes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy to support their development.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved 5th fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine, with a small number having hip dysplasia or delayed closure of the soft spot on the head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and address any dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss and address any hearing difficulties.
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems and provide appropriate correction or therapy.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Speech therapy to support the patient's communication development and address any speech difficulties.
* Occupational therapy to support the patient's fine motor development and address any feeding or sensory issues.
* Physiotherapy to support the patient's gross motor development and address any mobility or coordination concerns.
* Behavioural therapy to support the patient's behavioural development and address any anxiety or ADHD symptoms.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality in his heart, which requires regular check-ups to monitor its impact on his health and activity levels.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky and has issues with food texture, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally experiences blank spells where he just stares off into space and doesn't respond, which are unsettling to witness.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated in noisy environments and loud sounds seem to overwhelm him easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means his eyes are slightly crossed, and has been noticeable since he was a toddler.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, especially when eating cold foods, which causes him discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has language development issues, with limited verbal communication for his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with food texture and is extremely picky, and also experiences blank spells.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has undescended testicles, which are still under observation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as hypermetropia
* Cardiac review to monitor the valve abnormality and its impact on health and activity levels
* Neurological review to understand and manage the blank spells
* Speech therapy to address language development issues
* Occupational therapy to address feeding difficulties and food texture issues
* Behavioural therapy to address any behavioural differences or anxiety
* Regular monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints and experiences eye pain when looking at things for too long.
